articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities and individuals connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). These actions aim to counter illicit activities and human rights abuses in these regions.

For North Korea, the sanctions target government-run schemes that utilize IT workers to defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for Pyongyang's weapons programs. The targeted entity is the First Financial and Technical Development Center, along with six associated individuals based in North Korea and Russia.

The specific details regarding the Democratic Republic of the Congo designations were not immediately available in the initial announcement, but typically involve individuals or entities engaged in corruption, human rights abuses, or destabilizing activities within the region.

The updated FAQs likely address common compliance challenges and offer further interpretation of OFAC's requirements for handling blocked or rejected transactions, as well as the procedures for submitting the necessary reports.
Entities are encouraged to review the amended FAQs to ensure their internal compliance programs and reporting practices align with the latest OFAC guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran and Russia General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of significant actions on October 21, 2026, including new Iran-related designations, the removal of certain Belarus and North Korea designations, and the issuance of new and amended general licenses related to Iran and Russia.

The Iran-related designations target individuals and entities involved in activities contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. Concurrently, OFAC issued new Iran-related general licenses and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions to provide guidance on permissible activities.

In a notable development, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a potential shift in policy or a response to changed circumstances in those regions. Additionally, new Russia-related general licenses were issued, further refining the scope of authorized transactions under the Russia sanctions program.

Accompanying these designations, OFAC also issued associated General Licenses to mitigate unintended consequences and provide guidance on permissible activities involving the newly sanctioned parties.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to safeguarding American innovation and intellectual property from foreign adversaries and illicit actors.

articles.headline: Bank of America, N.A. Fined $11,662,930 by OFAC
body: Bank of America, N.A. has been assessed a civil penalty of $11,662,930 by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This penalty is part of coordinated enforcement actions for violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws.

The penalty stems from deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, including failures to properly monitor trillions of dollars in transactions, resulting in numerous late suspicious activity reports (SARs).

This action by OFAC, in coordination with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), underscores the serious consequences for financial institutions that fail to maintain effective sanctions and AML compliance programs.

articles.headline: ECB Maintains Key Interest Rates Amid Rising Energy Prices and Inflation Risks
body: The Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB) decided on October 29, 2026, to keep the three key ECB interest rates unchanged. The interest rates on the deposit facility, main refinancing operations, and marginal lending facility will remain at 2.50%, 2.65%, and 2.90% respectively.

This decision comes as energy prices continue to rise, posing upside risks to the inflation outlook and downside risks to economic growth. While the full effects of the energy shock are still unfolding, underlying inflation has remained broadly stable, and wages have not shown a material response.

The ECB reiterated its commitment to setting monetary policy to ensure inflation stabilizes at its 2% target in the medium term, emphasizing a data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting approach. The Governing Council also noted that financing conditions have tightened since its last meeting, which is likely to weigh on inflation and growth.

articles.headline: Cuba Accuses U.S. of Threatening Nations Ahead of UN Embargo Vote
body: Cuba has accused the United States of threatening countries with tariffs, visa restrictions, and other retaliatory measures to influence their votes on an upcoming United Nations resolution condemning the long-running U.S. embargo against the island.

Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla stated on October 21, 2026, that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Washington's ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, were personally leading a campaign to pressure UN General Assembly members to vote against the resolution.

The UN General Assembly has historically voted overwhelmingly in favor of non-binding resolutions calling for an end to the U.S. economic embargo on Cuba, which has been in place for over six decades. The allegations come amid escalating tensions and increased U.S. pressure on Cuba, including blocking oil supplies and threatening tariffs on countries supplying fuel to the island.

articles.headline: UFLPA Entity List Updated with Three New Additions Targeting Forced Labor in Xinjiang
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced an update to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List on October 29, 2026, adding three new entities. This update supersedes the previous UFLPA Entity List published on August 3, 2026.

The newly added entities are identified under UFLPA Section 2(d)(2)(B)(ii), which targets entities working with the government of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor, or receive forced labor or members of persecuted groups out of Xinjiang.

The updated UFLPA Entity List, included as an appendix to the Federal Register notice, is also available on the DHS website. This action reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to combating forced labor in supply chains linked to Xinjiang.

body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today released enforcement actions for October 2026.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes $750 Million Assessment Against Bank of America for Deficient BSA/AML Compliance
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Civil Money Penalty Against American Express
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah (bank), for deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.
